premises: Trace oxygen doping (~0.5 at%) during melting of HfZrTiTa0.53 can be controlled to form nanoscale oxide precipitates at grain boundaries.
Nanoscale oxide precipitates at grain boundaries blunt crack initiation and arrest intergranular crack propagation.
Blunting cracks and arresting propagation enhances tensile ductility and uniform elongation without reducing yield strength.
The intervention does not reduce impact-triggered chemical energy release relative to the baseline alloy.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a tensile strain of 13.5% at room temperature and ~10⁻³ s⁻¹.
